theme_zh: 在會議上報告數字與預測
summary_zh: 學會在會議上報告業績與預測時，用現在進行式／be going to／will 清楚區分「已排定的計畫」「已決定的打算」和「只是預測」，讓主管不會把估計當成承諾。

vocab.definition: an estimate of what a number will be in the future, based on current data
vocab.example: Our sales projection for next year assumes no new competitors.
vocab.example_zh: 我們明年的銷售預測是假設不會有新的競爭對手。

vocab.zh: 逐步加大、提高（投入或產量）
vocab.definition: to increase the amount or speed of something, usually step by step
vocab.example: We're going to ramp up hiring once the new office opens.
vocab.example_zh: 新辦公室開了之後，我們會逐步加快招募。

vocab.zh: （公司或部門的）人力編制、員額
vocab.definition: the number of people employed by a company or team
vocab.example: We can't take on the project without more headcount.
vocab.example_zh: 沒有增加人力編制，我們接不了這個專案。

vocab.definition: to earn exactly as much money as you spend, so there is no profit and no loss
vocab.example: The new store should break even in its second year.
vocab.example_zh: 新門市應該會在第二年打平。

vocab.definition: to look at data or a problem in more detail to find the cause
vocab.example: Let's drill down into the numbers by region.
vocab.example_zh: 我們按地區深入看一下這些數字。

vocab.definition: the most important point that you want people to remember
vocab.example: The key takeaway is that customers want faster delivery, not lower prices.
vocab.example_zh: 最重要的結論是：顧客要的是更快出貨，而不是更低的價格。

vocab.definition: compared with the same period in the previous year
vocab.example_zh: 線上訂單比去年同期成長了 25%。

vocab.definition: a situation or condition that makes progress more difficult
vocab.example: Higher shipping costs were a major headwind this quarter.
vocab.example_zh: 運費上漲是這一季主要的不利因素。

reading.title: Presenting a Forecast Without Losing the Room
paragraphs: Last quarter, Daniel's team launched a new subscription plan, and next Tuesday, when the quarterly review kicks off, he's presenting the first results. He has given this kind of presentation before. Two years ago, he learned a lesson the hard way: nobody remembers a slide full of numbers. What people remember is the story behind them.

So this time, he's going to open with one key takeaway: sign-ups are up 18% year-over-year, but revenue per user has dropped. Then he'll drill down into the reasons. Most new customers chose the cheapest plan, and a big competitor cut its prices in September, which created a headwind nobody had planned for.

The trickiest part will be the projection. Daniel's model shows that the new plan will break even in about eight months, but only if the team ramps up its marketing in the spring. He's careful with his wording here. When something is already arranged, he says so: "We're launching the spring campaign on March 3rd." When it's a decision the team has made, he uses "going to": "We're going to focus on annual plans." And when it's only a prediction, he says "we'll probably" or "I think it will," so nobody mistakes a guess for a promise.

He has also prepared for the question he knows is coming: headcount. The plan doesn't need new hires yet, but if sign-ups keep growing at this rate, the support team will need two more people by summer. Rather than wait to be asked, he's going to raise it himself. Then he'll close with the deliverables each team owes before the next review.
His goal is simple. When the meeting ends, he wants every manager to be able to repeat the main message in one sentence.

questions.q: What is the key takeaway Daniel plans to open with?
options: Sign-ups have grown, but each user is bringing in less money
The new plan has already broken even
A competitor has gone out of business
The support team needs two new people right away
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：「sign-ups are up 18% year-over-year, but revenue per user has dropped.」註冊人數成長，但每位用戶帶來的營收下降。

questions.q: According to Daniel's model, what has to happen for the plan to break even in about eight months?
options: The competitor has to raise its prices again
The team has to ramp up its marketing in the spring
The company has to hire more support staff
Customers have to switch to the cheapest plan
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：「will break even in about eight months, but only if the team ramps up its marketing in the spring.」

questions.q: Why does Daniel say "we'll probably" when he talks about predictions?
options: Because he isn't sure the presentation is on Tuesday
Because he wants to sound more confident
So the managers don't treat his estimates as commitments
Because the spring campaign has been cancelled
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：第三段結尾「so nobody mistakes a guess for a promise」——加上 probably，是為了讓主管知道這只是預測，不是保證。

grammar.point: Future forms: will, going to, present continuous for plans
grammar.point_zh: 未來式：will、be going to、現在進行式表示已安排的計畫
grammar.explain_zh: 三種未來說法看「這件事確定到什麼程度」：已經排進行事曆、有時間地點的安排 → 現在進行式（We're meeting the client on Friday.）；已經決定要做的打算，或從眼前證據推測 → be going to（I'm going to raise it myself. ／ Look at these numbers—we're going to miss the target.）；說話當下才決定、答應別人、或一般預測（常配 probably、I think）→ will（I'll send it now. ／ I think it'll take eight months.）。對照組：電話響了 ✓ I'll get it.（當下決定）✗ I'm going to get it.；行程已排好 ✓ I'm flying to Tokyo on Monday. 比 I will fly… 自然。形式別漏字：✓ I'm going to + 原形，✗ I going to／I'm going raise／I will to raise。
grammar.pattern: be + V-ing（已排定）／ be going to + V（已決定的打算、有證據的預測）／ will + V（當下決定、承諾、一般預測）

examples.en: We're launching the spring campaign on March 3rd.
examples.zh: 我們 3 月 3 日推出春季活動。（已經排定）

examples.en: I'm going to open the presentation with one key takeaway.
examples.zh: 我打算用一個重點結論開場。（已經決定）

examples.en: I think the new plan will probably break even by July.
examples.zh: 我想新方案大概會在七月前打平。（預測）

options: 'll get
'm going to get
'd get
get
exercises.explain_zh: 電話剛響、說話當下才決定去接 → 用 will（I'll get it）。going to 是事先就決定好的打算，這裡不自然。

exercises.q: Which is the most natural? "I ___ the vendor at 10 tomorrow — it's already on my calendar."
options: meet
'm meeting
'll meet
'd meet
exercises.explain_zh: 已經排進行事曆、有時間的安排 → 現在進行式 I'm meeting。I'll meet 文法上不算錯，但聽起來像當下才決定，最自然的是 'm meeting。

exercises.q: Look at these numbers. We ___ (miss) our Q4 target unless something changes.
exercises.explain_zh: 看著眼前的數字（證據）做預測，最常用 be going to：We're going to miss… 主詞 we 要配 are，別漏掉 be 動詞。will miss 也可以接受。

exercises.q: I think the new plan ___ even by next summer.
options: will break
is breaking
breaks
is going break
exercises.explain_zh: I think + 一般預測 → will + 原形動詞（will break even）。is breaking 是已排定的安排，「打平」不是能排進行事曆的事；breaks 用現在簡單式講個人預測不自然；is going break 少了 to（要說 is going to break even）。

exercises.q: Sorry, I can't make Thursday. I ___ (fly) to Tokyo that morning — the tickets are booked.
exercises.explain_zh: 機票已經訂好、行程確定 → 現在進行式 I'm flying 最自然（be going to fly 也可以）。

options: I'm going to raise the headcount issue myself.
I going to raise the headcount issue myself.
I'm going raise the headcount issue myself.
I will to raise the headcount issue myself.
exercises.explain_zh: be going to + 原形動詞，三個部分都不能少：I'm（be 動詞）＋ going to ＋ raise。will 後面直接接原形，不加 to。

review.point_zh: 現在完成式 vs 過去簡單式：「到現在」用完成式，「過去某個時間點」用過去式

exercises.q: Sign-ups ___ (grow) by 18% since we launched the new plan.
exercises.explain_zh: since + 過去時間點，表示「從那時到現在」→ 現在完成式 have grown。主詞 sign-ups 是複數，用 have。

exercises.q: We ___ the new pricing in September.
options: launched
have launched
have been launching
had launch
exercises.explain_zh: in September 是明確的過去時間點 → 過去式 launched。有時間點就不用完成式。

exercises.q: I ___ on this team for three years, so I know the numbers well.
options: worked
have worked
am working
work
exercises.explain_zh: for three years 而且現在還在這個團隊（so I know the numbers well）→ 現在完成式 have worked。用 worked 會變成「以前待過、現在不在了」。

listening.title: A quick dry run

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Sophie, do you have ten minutes? I'm presenting the Q3 numbers to leadership on Tuesday. Could we do a quick dry run?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Sophie
lines.text: Sure. So what's your key takeaway?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Sign-ups are up eighteen percent year-over-year, but revenue per user has gone down. I'm going to open with that.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Sophie
lines.text: Good. They'll definitely ask why revenue per user dropped, though.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: I know. I'll drill down into it on the second slide. Most new customers picked the cheapest plan.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Sophie
lines.text: And the projection? When does the plan break even?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: In about eight months, as long as we ramp up marketing in the spring.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Sophie
lines.text: Then say that clearly. If you just say "eight months," they'll hear it as a promise.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Fair point. I'll say we'll probably break even by July, if the spring campaign performs the way we expect.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Sophie
lines.text: Much better. Oh, and are you going to mention headcount?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Yes. Support is going to need two more people by summer if this keeps up. I'll bring it up before they do.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Sophie
lines.text: Smart. And finish with the deliverables for each team, so everyone leaves knowing what's next.

questions.q: When is Daniel presenting to leadership?
options: This afternoon
On Tuesday
In the spring
In July
questions.explain_zh: Daniel 一開始就說：「I'm presenting the Q3 numbers to leadership on Tuesday.」（現在進行式表示已排定的行程）

questions.q: What is Sophie worried about when Daniel just says "eight months"?
options: That the number is too low
That leadership will take it as a promise
That the slide will be too long
That marketing won't agree to it
questions.explain_zh: Sophie 說：「If you just say "eight months," they'll hear it as a promise.」只講數字，主管會當成保證。

questions.q: Why does Daniel most likely want to bring up headcount himself?
options: He wants to cancel the spring campaign
He has already hired two new people
He expects the question and would rather raise it on his own terms
Sophie told him not to mention it
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：他說「I'll bring it up before they do.」——他知道主管一定會問，先主動提出可以掌握說明的方式。

dictation: I'm presenting the Q3 numbers to leadership on Tuesday.
In about eight months, as long as we ramp up marketing in the spring.
Support is going to need two more people by summer if this keeps up.

shadowing: I'm presenting the results to the leadership team next Tuesday.
The key takeaway is that sign-ups are up year-over-year.
I think we'll probably break even by July.
I'm going to raise the headcount issue myself.

prompts.question: What are your plans for next week at work? Mention one thing that's already scheduled, one thing you've decided to do, and one prediction.
prompts.question_zh: 你下週工作上有什麼安排？說一件已經排定的事、一件你已決定要做的事，再加一個預測。
prompts.sample: On Monday, I'm meeting our biggest client to go over the contract. After that, I'm going to finish the budget for next year, because my manager needs it by Wednesday. I think the week will probably be busy, but if the meeting goes well, Friday should be a bit quieter.

prompts.question: Imagine you're presenting your team's numbers. Give the key takeaway and one projection, and make it clear which part is a prediction.
prompts.question_zh: 想像你在報告團隊的數字：說出最重要的結論和一個預測，並清楚表明哪一部分只是預測。
prompts.sample: The key takeaway is that orders are up twelve percent year-over-year, mainly thanks to online sales. Our projection shows that we'll probably reach our annual target in December, as long as shipping costs don't go up again. That part is an estimate, not a promise, so I'll update you next month.

writing.task: Write a short message (about 80–100 words) to your manager about a presentation you're giving next week. Say when it is, what you're going to cover, and give one prediction about the numbers.
writing.task_zh: 寫一則簡短訊息（約 80–100 字）給主管，說明你下週要做的簡報：什麼時候、打算講哪些內容，並對數字做一個預測。
writing.sample: Hi Karen, just a quick update on next week. I'm presenting our Q3 results to the regional team on Thursday at 2 p.m. I'm going to start with the key takeaway: sales are up 10% year-over-year, mainly because of our new online store. Then I'll drill down into the regions that are still behind. For Q4, I think we will probably hit our target, but only if the year-end promotion starts on time. I'll send you the slides on Tuesday so you can check them first. Thanks, Vincent
checklist_zh: 用 I'm presenting… on + 時間 說出已排定的簡報
用 I'm going to… 說明你決定要講的內容
用 will probably 做一個預測，並說明條件（if／as long as）
結尾說下一步（例如什麼時候寄簡報）

translation.zh: 我們下週二要跟客戶開會，已經排好了。
translation.en: We're meeting the client next Tuesday. It's already scheduled.
alt: We're meeting with the client next Tuesday; it's already been scheduled.
We have a meeting with the client next Tuesday. It's already set up.

translation.zh: 我覺得新方案大概會在明年夏天打平。
translation.en: I think the new plan will probably break even next summer.
alt: I think the new plan is probably going to break even next summer.
I think the new plan will probably break even by next summer.

translation.zh: 我們九月推出了新價格，從那之後註冊人數已經成長了 18%。
translation.en: We launched the new pricing in September, and sign-ups have grown by 18% since then.
alt: We launched the new prices in September, and since then sign-ups have gone up 18%.
We introduced the new pricing in September, and sign-ups have increased by 18% since then.

reading.title: When the Numbers Don't Cooperate
paragraphs: Every analyst has a nightmare scenario, and for Rachel Lin it arrived on a Thursday afternoon. Three days before the board meeting, the latest sales data came in well below forecast. Her deck, which she had spent two weeks polishing, was suddenly telling a story that was no longer true.

Her manager's first instinct was to soften the message. "Can't we just lead with subscriber growth and bury the revenue numbers on slide twelve?" he asked. Rachel understood the temptation, but she also knew the board. If they found the gap themselves, every other figure in the deck would lose credibility. Sugarcoating it wasn't going to make the problem go away; it was only going to make her look as if she'd been hiding it.

So she rebuilt the presentation around the elephant in the room. The opening slide stated the shortfall plainly; the next two explained what was driving it and what the team was going to do about it. Rather than offer a single revised forecast, she laid out three scenarios and was careful to label each one honestly. The cost-cutting measures were already decided — "we're closing the Denver warehouse at the end of January" — while the recovery numbers were explicitly projections: "if the new pricing lands the way we expect, revenue will probably stabilize by Q2."

The CFO pushed back hard, as Rachel had expected, asking why the original forecast had been so far off. She didn't get defensive. Instead, she walked the board through the assumption that had failed — a competitor's price cut nobody had seen coming — and admitted that the model had leaned too heavily on last year's data.

The meeting ran forty minutes over. But a week later, the CFO asked Rachel to present the quarterly numbers to the board herself, a job that had always belonged to her manager. Delivering bad news well, it turns out, can do more for your reputation than delivering good news.

questions.q: Why did Rachel refuse to bury the revenue numbers on slide twelve?
options: Her manager had told her to put them first
If the board noticed the gap on their own, they would stop trusting the rest of her figures
The board had asked to see revenue before anything else
She thought subscriber growth was not important
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：第二段「If they found the gap themselves, every other figure in the deck would lose credibility.」——被董事會自己發現，整份簡報的數字都會失去可信度。

questions.q: Which of these did Rachel present as already decided, not as a prediction?
options: Revenue stabilizing by Q2
The new pricing working as expected
Closing the Denver warehouse at the end of January
A competitor cutting its prices again
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：成本削減「already decided」，她用現在進行式「we're closing the Denver warehouse at the end of January」表示已確定；營收回穩則是 projection，用 will probably。

questions.q: What does the CFO's request a week later suggest?
options: He was impressed by how Rachel handled the bad news
He wanted to punish Rachel's manager for the missed forecast
He thought the meeting had been too long
He didn't believe Rachel's scenarios
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：會議後一週 CFO 請她親自向董事會報告季度數字（原本是她主管的工作），表示他欣賞並信任她處理壞消息的方式；最後一句也點出這一點。

listening.title: Bad news before the board meeting

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Greg, got a sec? I've just run the numbers again, and... yeah, it's not great.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Greg
lines.text: How not great are we talking?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: We're about twelve percent under forecast for the quarter. Maybe a bit more.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Greg
lines.text: Okay, okay. So, look — what if we just lead with subscriber growth and—

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: And leave the revenue for later? I thought about it, honestly. But the board's going to spot it in about five seconds.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Greg
lines.text: Yeah... Martin will, anyway. He reads every footnote.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Exactly. So I'm going to put it right up front, then walk them through three scenarios.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Greg
lines.text: Three? Isn't that a bit — I don't know — wishy-washy?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Not if I'm clear about which parts are locked in. The warehouse closure's happening in January, period. The recovery's a projection.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Greg
lines.text: Hmm. Fair enough. Just don't let them pin you down to a single number.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Believe me, I won't. I'll give them a range and stick to it.

questions.q: How far below forecast are the quarter's numbers?
options: About five percent
About twelve percent, maybe more
Exactly twenty percent
They are on forecast
questions.explain_zh: Rachel 說：「We're about twelve percent under forecast for the quarter. Maybe a bit more.」

questions.q: What does Greg imply about Martin?
options: He won't come to the board meeting
He pays close attention to detail and will notice the gap
He prefers to hear about subscriber growth first
He wrote the original forecast
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：「He reads every footnote.」連註腳都會看，表示他非常注意細節，一定會發現營收的落差。

questions.q: Why does Rachel think three scenarios won't sound vague?
options: She will make it clear what is already decided and what is only a projection
She will only show the most optimistic scenario
Greg will present two of the scenarios
The board has asked for exactly three scenarios
questions.explain_zh: 她說：「Not if I'm clear about which parts are locked in.」——倉庫關閉是確定的（period），回穩只是預測，分清楚就不會顯得含糊。

dictation: The board's going to spot it in about five seconds.
The warehouse closure's happening in January, period.
I'll give them a range and stick to it.

glossary.zh: 粉飾、把壞事講得比較好聽
glossary.definition: to make something unpleasant sound better than it really is

glossary.zh: 大家都知道卻避而不談的問題
glossary.definition: an obvious problem that everyone is aware of but nobody wants to talk about
the amount by which something is less than what was expected or needed
not clear or firm; showing no strong opinion or decision
fixed or agreed, so it can no longer be changed

glossary.zh: （放在句尾）就這樣、沒什麼好討論的
glossary.definition: used at the end of a statement to show that it is final and not open to discussion
